summary: Harford County forestry tower installed 1939 on a state site; removed (date not found); the site is now a Forest Service work center and communications complex.

facts.status_note: Forestry tower removed; no removal date in the sources read

events.note: State Forester urged a fire tower for northwestern Harford County, with funds to come from citizens, the county commissioners and the State
State acquired the 1.67-acre site under a deed dated 10 February 1936
DNR gives 1939 as the forestry tower installation date

evidence.supports: State Forester urged a fire tower in northwestern Harford County
evidence.quote: Erection of a fire tower in the northwestern section of Harford county has been urged by State Forester F.W. Besley.

evidence.supports: tower would protect woodland on the headwaters of Deer Creek and the Gunpowder River
evidence.quote: Such a tower, he said, would protect important woodland areas on the headwaters of Deer Creek in Harford county and on Gunpowder River in Baltimore county.

evidence.supports: funds to come from citizens, county commissioners and the State
evidence.quote: He urged that the necessary funds be subscribed by interested citizens, the county commissioners and the State.

evidence.supports: forest warden began a campaign to raise backing
evidence.quote: Forest Warden Nelson W. Morse of Forest Hill has already started a campaign in his section to obtain financial backing.

evidence.supports: site is in the town of Madonna
state acquired site under deed dated 10 February 1936

evidence.quote: Forestry tower was removed years ago.

evidence.supports: three communications towers replaced by one tower for state, federal and local use
evidence.quote: Previously, three communications towers were present but have since been replaced by one tower for State agency, federal and local use.

evidence.supports: current use is a Forest Service regional work center and communications complex
evidence.quote: Current Use: Forest service regional work center and multi-use communications complex

evidence.supports: access by Madonna Road north from Norrisville Road to a working facility
evidence.quote: Access: North on Madonna Road from Norrisville Road, the facility site is on the right.

evidence.supports: listed as gone in the Maryland lookout list

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties: A Resource Document

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one February 1932 newspaper item plus the DNR 2007 property entry. No height, staffing, design or removal date found. The DNR table lists no forestry tower at Madonna and the site as the Madonna Work Center. The 1932 article only urged a tower; the link to the 1939 installation rests on the DNR date alone. Access is left without a level because the report does not describe public visits.
